domain_label: Learner Model & Adaptivity — Weakness Diagnosis (why the weakness is there)
purpose: A method for an adaptive study system to diagnose WHY a flagged concept is weak — separating a slip from a stable misconception, a missing prerequisite, or a retrieval-decay failure — by designing targeted probe questions, walking prerequisite back-off down the concept graph, maintaining a concept-by-concept confusion matrix for discrimination failures, and connecting easy-detection to lower repetition load through FSRS stability and difficulty, so every weakness becomes a stored {concept, cause, evidence, prescribed-fix} record; cited learning-science findings are stated as fact and every probe-design and threshold choice is tagged an estimate.
assumptions: single-user system: population-scale models (DKT) are noted as the population option but never built; all skill estimates come from per-concept BKT and Elo layered on the per-card FSRS memory model

the differential-diagnosis decision procedure, its ordering, and every numeric threshold in it are design synthesis tagged ESTIMATE; the mechanisms each step leans on (BKT slip probability, KST prerequisite structure, FSRS predicted recall, distractor-misconception tagging) are the cited FACTs

cited empirical findings (BKT/DKT/Elo/IRT formulas, the 85% rule, interleaving effect sizes, KST fringe diagnosticity) are stated as fact with their source named in the node prose; no exam statistic, pass rate or effect size is invented beyond what the research file verified
direct page fetches were egress-blocked for several primary hosts during grounding, so the exact Glicko rating-deviation update equations are carried as UNKNOWN and never hard-coded
exclusions: the FSRS memory-model formulas themselves (DSR stability/difficulty math, revlog schema, optimizer, leech mechanism) — owned by the spaced-repetition specialist and only referenced here
the concept-graph / prerequisite-ladder construction and book decomposition that the prerequisite back-off walks — owned by the flashcards/decomposition specialist

question-format rendering and answer-grading mechanics (spoken transcription, LLM grading rubrics) the probes are delivered through — owned by the question-types specialist; only the guessing-floor consequence is modeled here
the gamification / calendar-fill UI and the whole-system self-metrics scorecard beyond the single diagnosis-efficacy loop that closes this KB
training a population-scale Deep Knowledge Tracing model, which requires thousands of learners' interaction data unavailable to a one-user system

competency_questions.question: How is a concept promoted from a noisy low score to a weakness worth diagnosing, and how does estimate uncertainty gate that decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEAKNESS_FLAG_TRIGGER fires only when (low Elo theta OR BKT P(L) below threshold) AND the estimate's uncertainty is low, and UNCERTAINTY_GATING supplies a Glicko-RD-style per-concept uncertainty (with the exact Glicko equations flagged UNKNOWN/egress-blocked) to separate a real weakness from an under-sampled one

competency_questions.question: What are the four rival explanations for a wrong answer and what observable signature distinguishes each?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ERROR_TAXONOMY names E1 slip (isolated error amid correct history; BKT P(S)), E2 misconception (systematic same-wrong-distractor; VanLehn buggy rules), E3 missing prerequisite (fails item AND its prerequisites; KST surmise relation), E4 retrieval failure (prior success, long elapsed time, low FSRS R), each with its cited basis and the synthesis tag on the assembly

competency_questions.question: How is a slip ruled out before any deeper cause is diagnosed, and why first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SLIP_RULE_OUT re-asks the same concept within 1-2 days via a differently worded item; a pass classifies E1 and restores P(L) with no content intervention, citing that BKT already prices a single error as a slip via P(S) so it moves the posterior less than two errors do (threshold logic tagged estimate)

competency_questions.question: How does the system distinguish a retrieval-decay failure from a never-learned concept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETRIEVAL_DECAY_TEST checks the card history: prior successes plus a low FSRS predicted recall R at failure time classify E4 decay -> schedule fix (shorten interval / relearning), whereas a HIGH R at failure (recent success, early lapse) redirects to E2/E3 or a bad card; the FACT is that FSRS supplies the predicted R, the threshold logic is tagged estimate

competency_questions.question: How does prerequisite back-off locate the true, deeper weakness and where is assessment most diagnostic?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREREQUISITE_BACKOFF walks DOWN the concept graph asking 1-2 items per direct prerequisite and recurses to remediate the deepest failing prerequisite first then rebuild upward; KST_FRINGE_LOGIC states inner/outer fringe items have maximal diagnostic value (ALEKS/KST, FACT) and that surmise relation q<=q' means mastering q' implies q (Doignon & Falmagne 1985, FACT)

competency_questions.question: How does a misconception probe confirm a stable wrong model rather than thin encoding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MISCONCEPTION_PROBE asks MCQ items whose distractors are each tagged with a specific wrong idea (Eedi-style, FACT) and classifies E2 only when the learner repeatedly selects the SAME misconception-tagged distractor across >=2-3 items, remediating with a contrast card; random distractor choice is read as not-E2 (thin encoding or E3), with the count threshold tagged estimate

competency_questions.question: How does the confusion matrix expose discrimination failure between sibling concepts, and how does it drive interleaving?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFUSION_MATRIX maintains a concept-by-concept matrix M[i][j] counting 'asked about i, answered with j content' from tagged distractors or graded free/spoken answers, and flags high off-diagonal pairs as discrimination failure (an E2 subtype); INTERLEAVING_FROM_CONFUSION feeds exactly those confused pairs into interleaved practice, citing interleaving trains discrimination (Brunmair & Richter 2019 g=0.42; Rohrer 2020 61% vs 38%, d=0.83, FACT)

competency_questions.question: How are diagnostic probe items designed, and why is the MCQ guessing floor a caveat on the evidence they yield?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROBE_DESIGN specifies purpose-built probes per cause (varied-surface retest for E1, prerequisite items for E3, misconception-tagged MCQ for E2) as design synthesis tagged estimate, and MCQ_GUESSING_FLOOR states the IRT 3PL pseudo-guessing floor c (~0.25 for a 4-option MCQ, FACT) makes an MCQ correct weaker mastery evidence than typed/spoken free recall, so probe updates are weighted accordingly

competency_questions.question: In what order is the differential diagnosis run and why does the order matter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIFFERENTIAL_ORDER runs rule-out-slip (E1) first, then decay-vs-never-learned (E4), then prerequisite back-off (E3), then misconception probe (E2), then the confusion-matrix discrimination check, because cheaper/higher-prior explanations are excluded before expensive content interventions, with the whole ordering tagged estimate and the mechanisms cited

competency_questions.question: What is the cause-to-fix mapping and what does a completed diagnosis store?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAUSE_FIX_MAP maps E1->none/note-fatigue, E2->contrast cards + distractor-targeted MCQ, E3->back off + suspend downstream cards until prereq P(L) recovers, E4->FSRS relearning + leech-rewrite-if-chronic, each with its scheduler effect; WEAKNESS_RECORD stores {concept, cause in E1..E4, evidence, prescribed fix} as the 'why' the owner asked for

competency_questions.question: How is 'easy for the user' detected and converted into lower repetition load through FSRS?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONCEPT_EASINESS aggregates FSRS per-card difficulty D and stability S plus Elo theta over a concept-tag so low-D + high-S + theta>>d concepts are 'mastered-easy' and stop generating fresh drills and start with longer initial steps (the load reduction is emergent from FSRS, FACT, not a bolt-on); RATING_HONESTY_CHECK flags Easy-marked cards with long latency or later lapses as over-optimistic self-grading

competency_questions.question: How does the nightly batch run diagnosis and measure whether its own fixes actually worked?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NIGHTLY_DIAGNOSIS_BATCH (idempotent, order-sensitive) recomputes the confusion matrix, flags concepts, runs the differential procedure as far as data allows, and emits a few probe items into tomorrow's queue so diagnosis never crowds out learning; DIAGNOSIS_EFFICACY_LOOP checks whether theta/P(L) recovered within K days of a fix and, if a fix class chronically fails, adjusts the diagnosis thresholds (the loop that improves the loop)

competency_questions.question: How does prerequisite remediation rebuild a blocked concept upward once the deepest failing base is found?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REMEDIATION_LADDER treats the surface concept as blocked, remediates the deepest failing prerequisite first, then rebuilds upward along the terminology -> basics -> two-relations -> multi-step ladder (owner terminology), suspending downstream cards until the prerequisite P(L) recovers per CAUSE_FIX_MAP's E3 scheduler effect

glossary.definition: The stored output of a completed diagnosis: {concept, cause in {E1 slip, E2 misconception, E3 missing prerequisite, E4 retrieval decay}, evidence, prescribed fix} — the 'why this weakness is there' the owner asked for, written to the learner KB.

The four rival explanations for a wrong answer: E1 slip (knows it, fumbled), E2 misconception (stable wrong model), E3 missing prerequisite (never had the base), E4 retrieval failure (learned then decayed); each has a distinct observable signature and a cited theoretical basis, while the assembly of the four into one taxonomy is design synthesis.

Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (Corbett & Anderson 1995) models one skill as a latent binary known/not-known state with four parameters P(L0), P(T), P(G), P(S); P(S) is the slip probability that a mastered learner still errs, which is exactly what makes a single wrong answer weak evidence of non-mastery [FACT].

The FSRS memory model's predicted probability of recall at a given moment given card stability S and elapsed time; a low R at failure time means the item was overdue (decay, E4), a high R at failure means the failure is early/unexpected and points at E2/E3 or a bad card [FACT that FSRS supplies R; the threshold reading is estimate].

Knowledge Space Theory (Doignon & Falmagne 1985): the surmise relation q <= q' means mastering q' implies having already mastered prerequisite q, so knowledge states form a prerequisite-respecting family; this is the structure prerequisite back-off walks downward [FACT].

In KST/ALEKS, the fringe of a knowledge state is where assessment is most informative: inner-fringe items (whose removal leaves a valid state) and outer-fringe items (addable next) are 'one step ahead' and carry maximal diagnostic value, so probes target the fringe rather than deep-known or far-unreachable items [FACT].

An MCQ answer option deliberately authored to encode one specific wrong idea (the Eedi-style design), so that WHICH distractor a learner picks is diagnostic; repeated selection of the same tagged distractor is the signature of a stable misconception E2 [FACT].

A matrix M where M[i][j] counts 'asked about concept i, answered with concept j's content' (from tagged distractors or graded free/spoken answers); high off-diagonal pairs are discrimination failure between siblings (a subtype of E2), remediated by direct-comparison items and interleaving of exactly that pair [bookkeeping is standard-ML applied here, estimate].

In the 3-parameter-logistic IRT model P(correct|theta)=c+(1-c)/(1+e^{-a(theta-b)}), c is the pseudo-guessing lower asymptote; for a 4-option MCQ random guessing gives c~0.25, so an MCQ correct is weaker mastery evidence than typed/spoken free recall and diagnostic updates are weighted down accordingly [FACT].

A concept-tag whose aggregated FSRS difficulty D is low, median stability S is high, and Elo theta far exceeds item difficulty d; such concepts get longer initial steps and stop drawing fresh drill items, so the repetition-load reduction the owner wants is emergent from FSRS rather than a separate feature [FACT for the FSRS dials].

Glicko (Glickman 1995) extends Elo with an explicit uncertainty (RD) around each rating that grows during inactivity and shrinks with play, mapping to 'how sure are we this weakness is real vs under-sampled'; the RD CONCEPT is cited FACT, but the exact Glicko update equations are UNKNOWN here because the canonical glicko.net spec was egress-blocked and must not be hard-coded from memory.

Bjork's desirable difficulties (spacing, interleaving, retrieval practice, generation) enhance long-term retention though they feel harder [FACT]; Wilson et al. 2019 (Nat. Commun. 10:4646) show ~85% training accuracy (optimal error 15.87% = Phi(-1)) maximizes learning rate for gradient-descent binary classifiers [FACT], used here as a principled default acquisition target, not a human law [scope reading is estimate].

nodes.definition: Establish the estimator substrate every weakness judgment reads from: per-concept skill models layered on top of the per-card FSRS memory model. Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (Corbett & Anderson 1995) models one skill as a latent binary state with four parameters P(L0)/P(T)/P(G)/P(S), fit by EM/Baum-Welch, giving an interpretable P(knows concept) from the first handful of answers and assuming no forgetting (which is why FSRS is still needed) [FACT]. Elo (Pelanek 2016) rates a learner theta per concept AND an item difficulty d at once with p=1/(1+e^-(theta-d)), theta<-theta+K(y-p), d<-d-K(y-p), K~0.4, O(1) updates [FACT]; it is a streaming approximation of Rasch/1PL IRT [FACT]. Deep Knowledge Tracing (Piech 2015, AUC 0.85 vs 0.68 BKT on Khan) is the population-scale option and is NOT built for a single user [FACT + design synthesis]. This node supplies the theta/P(L)/d signals the rest of the KB diagnoses.

nodes.definition: Establish the four rival explanations a flagged weakness must be sorted into, each with its observable signature and cited basis. E1 SLIP: knows it, fumbled — an isolated error amid a correct history on the same concept; BKT's P(S) is exactly this [FACT]. E2 MISCONCEPTION: a stable wrong model — systematic, reproducible wrong answers that pick the same wrong-idea distractor repeatedly; VanLehn's Repair Theory frames errors as systematic application of 'buggy' procedures [FACT]. E3 MISSING PREREQUISITE: never had the base — fails the item AND its prerequisite items, with errors clustering along prerequisite edges; grounded in KST's surmise relation (Doignon & Falmagne 1985) [FACT]. E4 RETRIEVAL FAILURE: learned then decayed — previously correct, long since, with FSRS predicted recall R low at failure [FACT by FSRS definition]. The four causes are mutually informative, not exclusive; assembling them into one taxonomy is design synthesis [ESTIMATE, high confidence]. This node is the diagnostic vocabulary every downstream test refines.

This is the first stage of the differential order and the guard against over-diagnosing one-off errors.

nodes.definition: Weight the evidence a probe yields by its format's guessing floor. In IRT's 3PL model P(correct|theta) = c + (1-c)/(1+e^{-a(theta-b)}), the pseudo-guessing lower asymptote c is the chance a learner with no ability still answers correctly; for a 4-option MCQ random guessing gives c ~ 0.25 [FACT]. Consequence: a 'correct' on a 4-option MCQ is ~25% expected by chance, so mastery evidence from an MCQ correct is WEAKER than from a typed or spoken free-recall answer, and diagnostic updates (to P(L), theta, and the confusion matrix) are weighted down for MCQ corrects accordingly. This makes free-recall probes preferable where mastery evidence must be firm, and it caps how much a lucky MCQ pass can raise a flagged concept. The c ~ 0.25 value is cited fact; the exact update-weighting is design synthesis [ESTIMATE].

conflict_axes.description: A failure on a previously-correct item can be retrieval decay (E4) or a missing prerequisite (E3), which prescribe a schedule fix versus a content fix.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read FSRS predicted R at failure: low R -> decay/schedule fix; high-R early lapse -> prerequisite back-off or bad card

conflict_axes.name: misconception_vs_thin_encoding
conflict_axes.description: Repeated errors can be a stable wrong model (E2) or merely thin/random encoding, distinguished only by consistency of the wrong choice.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: classify E2 only on the SAME misconception-tagged distractor across >=2-3 items; random choice is thin encoding or E3

conflict_axes.name: probe_budget_vs_learning_time
conflict_axes.description: Diagnostic probes compete with new-material and review for the daily queue, so more diagnosis means less learning.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: emit only a few probes per day from the nightly batch and diagnose over several nights rather than in one session

conflict_axes.name: mcq_correct_vs_free_recall_evidence
conflict_axes.description: An MCQ correct is cheap to collect but carries a guessing floor, while free recall is stronger evidence but costlier to grade.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight MCQ-correct evidence down by the ~0.25 guessing floor and prefer free-recall probes where mastery must be firm

conflict_axes.name: flag_sensitivity_vs_undersampling
conflict_axes.description: Flagging weaknesses early catches gaps sooner but risks acting on under-sampled concepts whose low score is just noise.
poles: flag early on a low score
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require (low theta OR low P(L)) AND low uncertainty; route high-uncertainty low scores to more probing, not diagnosis

conflict_axes.name: interpretability_vs_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: BKT/Elo are interpretable and work from little data, while DKT is more accurate but opaque and needs thousands of learners.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: for a single-user system use interpretable BKT/Elo and note DKT only as the population-scale option; do not build it

conflict_axes.name: easy_detection_vs_desirable_difficulty
conflict_axes.description: Cutting repetition on mastered-easy concepts saves time but can undercut the desirable difficulty that produces durable retention.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reduce load only for concepts that are mastered-easy and not confused; keep interleaving and retrieval practice for the rest

conflict_axes.name: surface_concept_vs_deepest_prerequisite
conflict_axes.description: Effort can go to the surface concept the learner wants or to the deepest failing prerequisite that actually blocks it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the surface concept as blocked, remediate the deepest failing prerequisite first, then rebuild upward

edge_cases.description: An isolated error amid a correct history is treated as a misconception without a varied-surface retest
edge_cases.trigger: the differential skips the slip stage and jumps to content remediation
edge_cases.mitigation: always run the E1 varied-surface retest first; require a second failure before deeper diagnosis

edge_cases.description: An early lapse with a HIGH predicted recall R is misclassified as retrieval decay
edge_cases.trigger: the decay test ignores R and assumes any lapse on a once-correct card is decay
edge_cases.mitigation: branch on FSRS R at failure: high R redirects to E2/E3 or a bad-card check rather than a schedule fix

edge_cases.description: Prerequisite back-off recurses without a floor and re-drills trivially-known basics
edge_cases.trigger: the recursion has no stop condition on already-mastered prerequisites
edge_cases.mitigation: target the fringe and stop the recursion at the first passing prerequisite layer

edge_cases.description: A misconception is declared from a single tagged-distractor pick or a single MCQ result
edge_cases.trigger: E2 is called before a repeated same-distractor pattern is established
edge_cases.mitigation: require the same misconception-tagged distractor across >=2-3 items and discount MCQ evidence by the guessing floor

edge_cases.description: A weakness is flagged on an under-sampled concept whose low score is just noise
edge_cases.trigger: the flag fires on a low score while the concept's uncertainty is high
edge_cases.mitigation: require low uncertainty alongside the low score and route high-uncertainty concepts to more probing

edge_cases.description: An off-diagonal confusion count comes from a grading error, not a real confusion
edge_cases.trigger: an LLM-graded free/spoken answer is mislabeled as the sibling concept's content
edge_cases.mitigation: require a sustained off-diagonal pattern and audit grading accuracy before interleaving a pair

edge_cases.description: Deep Knowledge Tracing is proposed for the single-user system
edge_cases.trigger: a push for higher AUC ignores that DKT needs thousands of learners' data
edge_cases.mitigation: keep interpretable BKT/Elo for one user and note DKT only as the population-scale option, not to be built

edge_cases.description: The exact Glicko rating-deviation update equations are hard-coded from memory
edge_cases.trigger: an implementer fills in the UNKNOWN Glicko math without fetching the primary spec
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the RD concept but use a labeled RD-like stand-in until the egress-blocked glicko.net spec is fetched; never hard-code from memory

edge_cases.description: The 85% success target is applied as a hard human law rather than a default
edge_cases.trigger: the ~85% figure from a learning-algorithm result is treated as a proven human RCT threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: use ~80-85% as a principled default acquisition target and keep it separate from the FSRS review-retention dial

edge_cases.description: Too many diagnostic probes are emitted and crowd out learning
edge_cases.trigger: the nightly batch queues a full differential re-test in one day
edge_cases.mitigation: cap probes at a few per day and diagnose across several nights so learning keeps priority

edge_cases.description: A card marked Easy has long response latency or later lapses, inflating concept easiness
edge_cases.trigger: the easiness aggregation trusts an over-optimistic self-grade
edge_cases.mitigation: discount Easy grades contradicted by the capped-60s revlog latency or later lapses before aggregating

edge_cases.description: Interleaving is forced on a concept's very first exposure and disrupts initial encoding
edge_cases.trigger: the no-blocking rule is applied before the first encounter is complete
edge_cases.mitigation: allow blocking only for the very first encounter, then interleave, per the mixed math results

workflow.action: Stand up the per-concept skill estimators
workflow.description: Run BKT per concept-tag and Elo (theta per concept, d per item) on the answer stream, noting DKT as out of scope
workflow.gate: BKT four-parameter and Elo dual-update estimates are produced with the no-forgetting caveat stated and DKT excluded

workflow.description: Carry a Glicko-RD-style uncertainty per concept, growing on inactivity, with the exact Glicko equations flagged UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: an RD-like uncertainty is attached and the exact Glicko equations are marked UNKNOWN with the egress-blocked source named

workflow.description: Flag concepts on (low theta OR low P(L)) AND low uncertainty and package the flag payload
workflow.gate: flags fire only on a well-measured low score and carry concept, estimates, uncertainty and recent history

workflow.description: Sort each flagged concept against E1 slip, E2 misconception, E3 missing prerequisite, E4 retrieval decay with their signatures
workflow.gate: the four causes are stated with cited bases and the assembly tagged synthesis

workflow.action: Rule out slip and test decay
workflow.description: Run the E1 varied-surface retest, then split E4 decay from never-learned via history and FSRS R
workflow.gate: a slip pass restores P(L) with no intervention and the decay test branches on FSRS R at failure

workflow.action: Back off to prerequisites at the fringe
workflow.description: Ask 1-2 fringe items per direct prerequisite and recurse to the deepest failing base
workflow.artifact: E3 verdict and deepest failing prerequisite
workflow.gate: the back-off targets the fringe and identifies the deepest failing prerequisite to remediate first

workflow.action: Probe for misconceptions and build the confusion matrix
workflow.description: Ask tagged-distractor MCQs, classify E2 on repeated same-distractor picks, and tally the concept-by-concept confusion matrix
workflow.gate: E2 is classified only on a repeated tagged-distractor pattern and off-diagonal pairs are recorded

workflow.action: Design and weight the probe items
workflow.description: Compose one probe shape per cause within a few-per-day budget and weight MCQ evidence by the guessing floor
workflow.gate: each cause has a discriminating probe and MCQ-correct evidence is weighted below free recall

workflow.action: Run the ordered differential and map to fixes
workflow.description: Sequence E1->E4->E3->E2->discrimination, emit a cause label, and look up its fix and scheduler effect
workflow.gate: the procedure runs cheapest-first, emits a labeled cause with evidence, and maps it to a fix with a scheduler effect

workflow.action: Store the weakness record and rebuild prerequisites
workflow.description: Write the append-only {concept, cause, evidence, fix} record and, for E3, rebuild upward along the terminology->multi-step ladder
workflow.gate: records are written as append-only data and E3 rebuild keeps downstream cards suspended until the prerequisite recovers

workflow.action: Detect easiness and check rating honesty
workflow.description: Aggregate FSRS D/S and Elo theta to mark mastered-easy concepts and discount over-optimistic Easy grades
workflow.gate: mastered-easy concepts lengthen steps and stop drills, and Easy grades contradicted by latency/lapses are discounted

workflow.action: Run the nightly batch and the efficacy loop
workflow.description: Idempotently cluster weaknesses, emit a few probes into tomorrow's queue, and check whether prior fixes restored theta/P(L)
workflow.artifact: nightly diagnosis output and efficacy snapshot
workflow.gate: the batch is safe to re-run, probes stay few-per-day, and the efficacy loop adjusts the procedure when a fix class chronically fails

priority_rationale: The skill-model substrate, uncertainty gating and weakness flag come first because every downstream test reads their theta/P(L)/uncertainty signals and no diagnosis is meaningful on noise; the error taxonomy then names the four rival causes the whole KB exists to distinguish; the per-cause tests (slip rule-out, decay-vs-never-learned, prerequisite back-off with fringe logic, misconception probe with the confusion matrix) and the probe design plus guessing-floor weighting are the diagnostic core; the differential order composes them cheapest-first into a single cause label, the cause-fix map and weakness record make that label actionable and auditable, and the remediation ladder and interleaving carry out the E2/E3 fixes; concept-easiness and the rating-honesty check convert mastery into lower repetition load through FSRS; and the nightly batch and the diagnosis-efficacy loop come last because they operationalize the whole procedure as an idempotent job that measures and corrects its own thresholds.

dominance_rules.rule: The slip rule-out dominates any deeper cause on a first single error
dominance_rules.rationale: BKT prices a single error as a possible slip via P(S), so one error is weak evidence of a stable cause
dominance_rules.trigger: a concept fails once amid a correct history
dominance_rules.action: run the varied-surface retest first and diagnose deeper only after a second failure

dominance_rules.rule: FSRS predicted R dominates the decay-vs-content decision
dominance_rules.rationale: a low R at failure means the item was overdue, so the fix is scheduling not content
dominance_rules.action: classify decay and schedule-fix when R was low; only a high-R early lapse licenses content back-off

dominance_rules.rule: The deepest failing prerequisite dominates the surface concept
dominance_rules.rationale: remediating a surface concept over a missing base rebuilds on a foundation that will not hold
dominance_rules.trigger: a failed concept has a failing direct prerequisite
dominance_rules.action: treat the surface concept as blocked and remediate the deepest failing prerequisite first, then rebuild upward

dominance_rules.rule: A repeated same-distractor pattern dominates a single wrong answer for E2
dominance_rules.rationale: one wrong pick can be noise or a guess, while a repeated tagged-distractor pattern is a stable wrong model
dominance_rules.action: classify E2 only on the same misconception-tagged distractor across >=2-3 items

dominance_rules.rule: Low uncertainty dominates a low score for flagging
dominance_rules.rationale: a low score on an under-sampled concept is noise, not a diagnosable weakness
dominance_rules.trigger: a concept shows a low theta or P(L)
dominance_rules.action: flag for diagnosis only when uncertainty is low; otherwise route to more probing

dominance_rules.rule: The guessing floor dominates raw MCQ correctness as mastery evidence
dominance_rules.rationale: a 4-option MCQ correct is ~25% expected by chance, so it is weaker evidence than free recall
dominance_rules.trigger: an MCQ correct would raise a flagged concept's mastery
dominance_rules.action: weight the MCQ-correct evidence down by the guessing floor and prefer free-recall confirmation

dominance_rules.rule: A few probes per day dominates thorough same-day diagnosis
dominance_rules.rationale: probes compete with learning for the queue, and learning has priority
dominance_rules.trigger: a weakness needs multiple probes to resolve
dominance_rules.action: emit a few probes per night and resolve the diagnosis across several days

dominance_rules.rule: A fetched primary spec dominates memory for the Glicko equations
dominance_rules.rationale: the exact Glicko update math is UNKNOWN here because the source was egress-blocked
dominance_rules.trigger: the RD-style uncertainty is to be implemented exactly
dominance_rules.action: use a labeled RD-like stand-in until glicko.net is fetched; never hard-code the equations from memory

dominance_rules.rule: Measured recovery dominates a plausible fix when adjusting the procedure
dominance_rules.rationale: a fix that does not restore theta/P(L) within K days is failing regardless of how sensible it seems
dominance_rules.trigger: a fix class is applied repeatedly
dominance_rules.action: track recovery per weakness record and adjust the diagnosis thresholds when a fix class chronically fails

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the slip rule-out before any content remediation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building contrast cards or prerequisite drills for what was a one-off fumble

anti_rework_rules.rule: Branch the decay test on FSRS R before choosing a fix
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rewriting content for an overdue review that only needed a schedule change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Require low uncertainty before flagging a weakness
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending a full differential on an under-sampled concept whose score was noise

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish a repeated same-distractor pattern before calling E2
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sending a learner down a contrast-card path for a random wrong pick or a guess

anti_rework_rules.rule: Weight MCQ evidence by the guessing floor when updating mastery
anti_rework_rules.prevents: clearing a flagged weakness on a lucky MCQ pass and re-flagging it later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the Glicko exact equations UNKNOWN until the primary spec is fetched
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping a hard-coded uncertainty that has to be ripped out when the real spec disagrees

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cap diagnostic probes at a few per day from the nightly batch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a diagnosis binge crowding out learning and having to rebuild the day's schedule

anti_rework_rules.rule: Discount over-optimistic Easy grades before aggregating concept easiness
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cutting repetition on a concept that only felt easy and then lapses

iteration_protocol.trigger: the glicko.net primary spec (or another fetchable source) provides the exact Glicko rating-deviation update equations
iteration_protocol.action: replace the labeled RD-like stand-in with the real equations and re-check the flag's low-uncertainty condition

iteration_protocol.trigger: the diagnosis-efficacy loop shows a fix class chronically fails to restore theta/P(L) within K days
iteration_protocol.action: adjust the differential-order thresholds, probe shapes, or flag cutoff and re-run the affected diagnoses

iteration_protocol.trigger: free/spoken answer grading accuracy is measured and shifts the reliability of confusion-matrix off-diagonal counts
iteration_protocol.action: re-weight the off-diagonal evidence and re-confirm which confused pairs are interleaved

iteration_protocol.trigger: the concept graph or prerequisite ladder is revised by the decomposition specialist
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the prerequisite back-off targets and the rebuild ladder order

iteration_protocol.trigger: the FSRS parameters are refit and change predicted R or the D/S distribution
iteration_protocol.action: re-tune the decay-vs-early-lapse R cutoff and the concept-easiness aggregation

iteration_protocol.trigger: observed MCQ success on unknown items diverges from the assumed ~0.25 guessing floor, or a new answer format is added
iteration_protocol.action: update the guessing-floor weighting and the probe-format choices that depend on it

iteration_protocol.trigger: the daily probe budget is found to crowd out learning or to starve diagnosis
iteration_protocol.action: re-balance the few-per-day probe cap in the nightly batch
